articles.title: TenZ Teams with Pulsar Gaming Gears for New Signature Wireless Mouse - Inven Global
articles.content:
Pulsar Gaming Gears has announced a new TenZ Signature Edition wireless gaming mouse, designed in collaboration with popular streamer and former professional esports player Tyson "TenZ" Ngo. The reveal came at the VALORANT Champions Tour (VCT) Americas Block Party on March 24, 2025. A limited quantity is currently available exclusively through the iBUYPOWER Gear Store, the official PC partner of VCT Americas.
TenZ, known for his precise aim and standout performance during his esports career, utilized his extensive experience to shape the design of this mouse, tailored specifically to his competitive playstyle. Pulsar Gaming Gears, the official mouse, keyboard, and mousepad partner of both VCT Americas and VCT Pacific, teamed up with TenZ to provide gamers with a mouse promising elite performance and precision.
Weighing only 47 grams, the TenZ Signature Edition mouse emphasizes speed and effortless control. It features Pulsar's Optical Switches rated for 100 million clicks, an XS-1 flagship sensor with up to 32,000 DPI, 750 inches per second (IPS), and an impressive 8K polling rate for enhanced responsiveness.
Additional highlights include battery life ranging from 18 to 112 hours based on polling rate, a sleek black-and-white design inspired by TenZ’s aesthetic, and an optimized shape specifically created by TenZ for claw grip gamers, which also ensures daily-use comfort.
The mouse initially retails for $130 at iBUYPOWER's gear store, with further availability expanding to Pulsar's own website and major retailers in April 2025. Customers interested in future restocks can sign up for notifications via iBUYPOWER's online product page. Pulsar Gaming Gears, headquartered in South Korea, continues its commitment to innovative esports technology, aiming to provide high-quality gear to gamers striving for peak performance.

articles.title: VALORANT Master Bangkok showmatch rosters revealed - Esports Insider
articles.content:
VALORANT has revealed the rosters for the upcoming ‘Thailand versus The World’ showmatch during the Masters Bangkok Grand Finals.
On March 2nd at 2 AM PST (10 AM GMT), the showmatch will see the likes of content creator Tyson ‘TenZ‘ Ngo and professional player Papaphat ‘Primmie’ Sriprapha showcase VALORANT’s new agent.
The showmatch and agent reveal ahead of the Grand Final series were initially announced on February 19th, with TenZ and Thai player Nattawat ‘SuperBusS‘ Yoosawat as captains for Team International and Team Thailand, respectively.
Today’s announcement confirmed that TenZ will be joined by his former Sentinels teammate Amine ‘johnqt’ Ouarid and Seina ‘KOHAL’ Migita.
KOHAL is a VALORANT streamer for Japanese esports organisation ZETA DIVISION, which also employs popular retired player and streamer Koji ‘Laz’ Ushida. The roster will be completed by former pro players Su ‘Karsaj’ Qifang and Ahn ‘Doenmo’ Seung-won.
SuperBusS’ roster will feature TALON player Primmie and Patiphan ‘CigaretteS/CGR’ Posri, a content creator for esports organisation Paper Rex. They will be joined by VALORANT streamer MintAuka and Thai artist Heart.Bus.
Masters Bangkok is taking place in the city’s UOB Live from February 20th until March 2nd. Featuring a $500,000 (~£404,400) prize pool, the VALORANT tournament has seen eight teams from around the globe fight through the Swiss Stage.
With four teams remaining, the double-elimination Playoffs are set to kick off tomorrow. Team Vitality, G2 Esports, T1 as well as 2024 Champions winner Edward Gaming (EDG) are still in the running to secure the first international trophy of VALORANT’s 2025 esports season.
The promotional campaign for the game’s upcoming Agent 28 has been running alongside Masters Bangkok, beginning with the event’s ‘Dawn of the Duelist’ cinematic, which hinted at the agent’s role as a duelist and their abilities.

articles.title: VALORANT Masters Bangkok: Zellsis discusses Sentinels expectations without TenZ - Esports Insider
articles.content:
Sentinels is set to compete in its fourth Masters event, VALORANT Masters Bangkok, following an outstanding performance at Americas Kickoff 2025.
However, for the first time, the team will set foot on the international stage without its star player, Tyson ‘TenZ’ Ngo, after he announced his retirement in 2024.
TenZ was the longest-serving member of Sentinels and the first North American player to win VALORANT Masters twice, both times with the American org. Establishing himself as one of the best duelists in his early VALORANT competitive career, he later transitioned into an impactful controller and initiator for the team.
In a pre-event press conference, Jordan ‘Zellsis’ Montemurro was asked about Sentinels’ expectations for VALORANT Masters Bangkok without TenZ being on the roster.
“I think we’re gonna be good,” Zellsis said. “I’ve said before in an interview that this Sentinels roster has the highest skill ceiling we’ve ever had in terms of potential.”
He continued: “Obviously, TenZ is a phenomenal player and an X-factor, but we have our own little X-factor here [looking towards N4RRATE], so that void is filled.”
Sentinels faced difficulties after the departures of TenZ and Sacy, struggling with consistency during the 2024 off-season. However, things eventually fell into place as the team secured its spot at Masters Bangkok, with young talents Marshall ‘N4RRATE’ Massey and Sean ‘Bang’ Bezerra stepping up to complete the roster.
“It’s amazing to qualify for Masters, especially considering the identity crisis we went through in the off-season while testing things,” said Zellsis.
“I think we got a little lucky with our roster moves, bringing in N4RRATE and Bang—both incredibly talented and hungry to win. Given the short time we’ve had as a team and how young we are, qualifying this early is a blessing. Honestly, I’m just happy to be here.”

articles.title: TenZ postpones VALORANT Community Awards until February 2026 - Esports Insider
articles.content:
VALORANT esports personality Tyson ‘TenZ‘ Van Ngo has postponed the inaugural edition of the VALORANT Community Awards Show until 2026.
The awards ceremony, announced in collaboration with Riot Games and Red Bull, was set to take place on December 15th in Los Angeles, California.
Revealed on November 19th, the VALORANT Community Awards Show is a live ceremony that celebrates both VALORANT Champions Tour (VCT) and Game Changers scenes.
Instead of taking place in December, the awards ceremony will take place on February 4th, 2026, at 9 PM PST (5 AM GMT). The reason for the postponement is to allow more individuals to attend the event in person. In addition to the new date, the former Sentinels player teased that the finalists for each category will be revealed soon.
“Hey everyone, we’re postponing the VALORANT Community Awards to February 4th so more people can attend on site,” said TenZ on social media. “Many are away for the holidays, and we want the best live show possible for everyone: players, teams, and fans at home!”
The VALORANT Community Awards Show is the second award ceremony affiliated with Riot Games’ first-person shooter title, acknowledging highlights from the 2025 VCT season. Riot Games’ 2025 VCT Awards took place on December 7th and shone a spotlight on its regional competitions. For VCT EMEA, Fnatic’s Kajetan ‘Kaajak’ Haremski won four awards (Player of the Year, Rookie of the Year, Duelist of the Year and Most Improved Player of the Year.)
For the Americas, Erick ‘aspas’ Santos (MIBR) won Player of the Year and Duelist of the Year, while Jason ‘f0rsakeN‘ Susanto (Paper Rex) won Player of the Year for the Pacific.
The Growth Of Awards Ceremonies
Several esports scenes are hosting end-of-year ceremonies to celebrate the best players from across the world. On December 19th, Riot Games will host the 2025 LCK Awards for League of Legends.
The developer and publisher also collaborated with Marc ‘Caedrel‘ Lamont for the League Awards 2025. Gen.G midlaner Jeong ‘Chovy‘ Ji-hoon took home the Player of the Year accolade.
Earlier this year, Supercell hosted the Clash Royale League (CRL) Awards, acknowledging top talent and best plays from across the mobile strategy title’s competitive scene.
Outside of esports-focused ceremonies, mainstream gaming awards shows continue to acknowledge esports players, organisations, and personalities. This year’s edition of The Game Awards features several esports categories, including the Best Esports Team, Best Esports Athlete, and Best Esports Game.

articles.title: TenZ and Alexis named in Forbes 30 Under 30 US Games list - Esports Insider
articles.content:
VALORANT content creator Tyson ‘TenZ‘ Van Ngo and esports player Alexis ‘alexis‘ Guarrasi are among the names featured in this year’s Forbes 30 Under 30 US Games list.
The list highlights the achievements of Alexis as a member of Shopify Rebellion Gold, alongside the accolades of retired VCT player TenZ during his time representing Sentinels.
Alexis is a 23-year-old VALORANT esports player and has competed in Riot Games’ first-person shooter title since 2020. Forbes stated that she is the highest-earning woman in VALORANT history, winning over $150,000 (~£112,900) in prize money over the last five years. In 2023 and 2024, she won back-to-back VCT Game Changers Championship titles.
“At a loss for words. Selected for the Forbes 30 Under 30 list. So honoured,” shared Alexis in a social media post. Alongside her playing career, Alexis recently launched a podcast with Shopify Rebellion Gold teammate Melanie ‘meL‘ Capone.
TenZ is widely regarded as one of the most popular VALORANT players in the history of the esport. In 2024, he achieved victory at Masters Madrid along with a top-four finish at VALORANT Champions. In September 2025, TenZ announced his retirement from professional play, making a transition to content creation.
The former champion remains heavily involved with VALORANT esports. In November, he launched a community awards show celebrating the VALORANT Champions Tour (VCT) and Game Changers scenes.
What Is Forbes 30 Under 30?
Every year, Forbes releases its ’30 Under 30′ and ’50 Under 50′ lists to highlight the contributions and achievements of individuals across a range of categories, including education, media, and finance. To earn a place on the lists, nominees are selected by a panel of expert judges.
TenZ and Alexis aren’t the only esports-adjacent personalities included on this year’s ‘Games’ list. Jordan Lazarus, founder of Xen Gaming, and Spencer Ma, Director of Growth at Carry1st, also feature among the alumni.
Elsewhere, Twitch streamer Emily ‘Emiru‘ Schunk features on the list. Forbes reveals that the 27-year-old cosplayer earned approximately $1.5m (~£1.1m) over the last 12 months.

articles.title: Kyedae and TenZ join the Game Changers Championship 2025 showmatch - Esports.gg
articles.content:
Your favorite streamers will face off in a 2v2 showmatch during the VALORANT Game Changers Championship 2025.
The VALORANT Game Changers Championship 2025 is approaching its finale, but before that, fans can enjoy a special showmatch on Nov. 29 featuring popular talent from every region. Kyedae “Kyedae” Shymko and Tyson “TenZ” Ngo will represent North America.
Game Changers Championship 2025 showmatch
Riot Games has revealed all the teams facing each other in the VALORANT Game Changers Championship 2025 showmatch set to happen on Nov. 29 at 12 a.m. PT / 3 a.m. ET / 5 p.m. KST. Your favorite streamers will be battling it out in a 2v2 skirmish showmatch, the latest game mode released in VALORANT.
Team Americas will feature the popular duo kyedae and TenZ. While TenZ has retired to be a full-time content creator, kyedae has stepped away from streaming. She has been playing for the Teevee, a Tier 2 NA VALORANT team. On Team EMEA, we will have Vivian “roxi” Schilling, former G2 Gozen and Karmine Corp GC player, alongside Lucas “HITBOX” González-Sabariegos, a streamer for GIANTX.
Representing the Pacific region will be Spicyuuu, the Singaporean streamer and former Paper Rex content creator. Additionally, Kim “972” Tae-il, founder of the Game Changers team Ninetails, who was recently eliminated from the tournament, will join her.
Finally, team China will be represented by AIJIANG, a popular Chinese streamer on Douyin (the Chinese TikTok), and Li “KMD” Zitao, former pro player of Kingzone and KeepBest Gaming.
Where can to watch the showmatch
You can watch all the Game Changers Championship 2025 matches and showmatch on the official VALORANT esports Twitch and YouTube channels. Watching the event on Twitch will reward two exclusive drops, the “Go Off” title, and the new KAY/O Punch spray.
In the Grand Finals, held on Nov. 30, there will be an opening ceremony featuring KATSEYE. They will be performing their anthem titled “M.I.A.”
That’s all for now. Stick around for more VALORANT news, guides, and updates on esports.gg.

articles.title: 'Pulsar TenZ Signature Edition Wireless' Gaming Mouse Announced, General April '25 Release - PlayDayOne

The TenZ Signature mouse features an optimal shape for claw grip users, a very long battery life of up to 112 hours (dependant on the polling rate), and one heck of a sleek look.
Have a gander below for more details on the Pulsar TenZ Signature Edition mouse. Prospective buyers can pick up their own units right now over at IBUYPOWER as well as Pulsar.gg later in April of 2025.

The mouse was created in collaboration with Pulsar Gaming Gears, allowing fans and aspiring competitive players to experience elite gaming performance with this new mouse validated by TenZ himself.
“After years of trying out tons of different mice both as an esports pro and as a streamer, I know exactly thet type of feel and responsiveness I demand when it comes to gaming mice, which is where Pulsar comes in,” said Tyson “TenZ” Ngo. “These guys live and breathe esports one hundred percent, so with their background and resources, it was a no-brainer on why I chose to work with them to deliver my dream gaming mouse for myself, and to my fans.”
Pulsar Gaming Gears is a leading esports brand founded in South Korea, and the Official Mouse, Keyboard, and Mousepad Partner of VCT Americas and VCT Pacific. The mouse comes equipped with Pulsar’s Optical Switches for a 100 million click lifestyle, its XS-1 flagship sensor that is capable of up to 32,000 DPI (Dots per Inch), 750 IPS (Inches per Second), and an 8K polling rate for unmatched responsiveness during gameplay.

It reinforced a core belief we have at Pulsar that everyone should have the right to gear fit for peak performance,” said Stuart Chan, CMO at Pulsar Gaming Gears. “The mouse is one of our most exciting products to date, and serves as a high benchmark for all future partnership products. TenZ was a true pleasure to work with and we’re looking forward to more potential collaborations in the future.”
iBUYPOWER will be the exclusive online retailer of the Pulsar TenZ Signature Edition wireless gaming mouse with initial availability of the new peripheral. Restocks are to be expected, so customers can click “Notify Me” on the product listing to be informed once new inventory arrives.

articles.title: “I’m back”: TenZ returns to VALORANT esports with Cubert Academy - Esports Insider
articles.content:
Tyson ‘TenZ‘ Ngo has officially announced his return to competitive VALORANT, joining Sentinels’ academy roster, Cubert Academy, as a last-minute substitute.
He’ll be filling in for Logan ‘skuba‘ Jenkins, who was recently transferred to NRG, until the organisation finds a replacement.
The VALORANT legend is set to make his VCT Challengers debut during the Stage 2 Playoffs, and will also stream his POV on his Twitch channel.
“Going to be subbing in playoffs for Cubert Academy, will be streaming my POV on my channels! Time to make my Challengers debut,” TenZ announced on X (Twitter).
TenZ will play his first match for Cubert Academy against Winthrop University on May 20th, in a best-of-three series. The matchup is expected to break viewership records for the Challengers League, with his fans extremely hyped for it.
The game will be streamed live on VCT North America’s official Twitch and YouTube channels, but viewers will also be able to tune in to the watch parties organized by multiple content creators.
The Return of Tenz
TenZ originally announced his retirement from professional VALORANT in 2024, staying with Sentinels as a content creator. He recently parted ways with the American organisation, but has now made a temporary return.
“I guess he’s back! When Sen needs a super sub there is only one man to call @TenZOfficial!” said Sentinels CEO Rob Moore, welcoming him back.
Cubert Academy will be starting its playoffs run in the Upper Quarterfinals of the double-elimination bracket. While the team has already qualified for Challengers North America Stage 3, it won’t earn any circuit points toward VCT Ascension Americas 2025 qualification.
This is because academy teams of VCT partnered organisations such as Sentinels are ineligible to qualify for Ascension tournaments. However, Cubert Academy are also protected from relegation, unlike other lower-ranking Challengers teams.

articles.title: TenZ returns to Valorant esports with Cubert Academy viewership - Esports Charts
articles.content:
TenZ returns to Valorant esports with Cubert Academy, and with his own POV stream of matches on YouTube and Twitch
TenZ, the favourite child of the North American Valorant scene, is back competing after retiring last year. The star player isn’t returning to the VCT, but will play for Sentinels’ academy team, Cubert Academy, for the reminder of the Challengers playoffs. TenZ’s presence could make the 2025 Stage 2 one of the most popular Challengers events ever.
On May 19, Cubert Academy announced Tyson “TenZ” Ngo’s return for the Valorant Challengers 2025 North America: Stage 2 playoffs. He replaces Logan "skuba" Jenkins, who recently joined NRG’s Valorant Champions Tour roster, replacing the retiring Pujan "FNS" Mehta. TenZ’s signing resembles Sentinels’ signing of Michael "shroud" Grzesiek in 2022; shroud played one event for Sentinels while they rebuilt their roster.
RETURN OF THE KING@TenZOfficial will be joining Cubert Academy for Stage 2 playoffs pic.twitter.com/aj2hzamo6D
— Cubert (@CubertAcademy) May 20, 2025
During his return to competition, TenZ will not only appear on other broadcasts, but TenZ will also stream his own POV of the matches on his channels to both his Twitch and YouTube channels. In the past, TenZ attracted over 100,000 concurrent viewers for his esports co-streams, so it will be interesting to see how his POV broadcasts compare.
TenZ's first match with Cubert Academy begins at 7 p.m. ET on May 20 against Winthrop. Challengers North America uses a double-elimination format for playoffs. This means TenZ will play at least two matches with the roster across this week and the next.
 
 
Broadcasting official matches and scrims has gained popularity recently in the streaming world. Hardcore fans love it, and casual fans are catching on. Everyone finds some interest in the insights these streams offer into competitive gaming.
In League of Legends, British co-streamer and caster Marc "Caedrel" Lamont streamed ‘scrims’ (practice matches) and games for his team Los Ratones, which exploded in popularity and set new records for various European tournament series. TenZ’s POV stream will give fans a unique insight into the world of Valorant esports. With such a beloved player like TenZ, this will likely be one of the biggest livestreamed Valorant events of the year for North American fans.
Read also: Scrims on streams: how the new rule can help League of Legends teams attract a new audience
But didn’t TenZ leave Sentinels? Yes, but not really. Earlier this month, TenZ announced on X that he officially parted ways with Sentinels, however, both the official Sentinels X account and their CEO Rob Moore said the split was to open more opportunities for TenZ. While a Sentinels-contracted player, his potential brand deals were limited due to conflicts with Sentinels’ sponsors. Now, he can explore a wider range of deals for his future as a content creator.
guys guys relax, it's just to not conflict with future sponsor deals. TenZ will always be Sentinels family
— Sentinels (@Sentinels) May 8, 2025
TenZ’s signing with Cubert Academy shows his bond with the Sentinels organization, even if they are no longer officially in business. Not only is this a happy day for TenZ fans, but with Cubert Academy and TenZ potentially going up against the dominant, streamer-team ENVY in their second game, this could be one of the most-watched Challengers games from North America ever.

articles.title: Valorant Star TenZ Is Red Bull Athlete Roster - The Esports Advocate
articles.content:
Tyson “TenZ” Ngo, one of esports’ most prominent figures, has officially joined Red Bull as a global athlete through a partnership brokered by Prodigy Agency, a talent representation firm in gaming and esports.
Widely considered “the face of Valorant,” TenZ boasts an extensive following exceeding 14 million across social platforms. Known for exceptional skill, creativity, and competitive accomplishments, TenZ’s new collaboration with Red Bull solidifies his position among an elite group of global athletes.
Red Bull’s strategy with esports ambassadors focuses on authentic lifestyle integration, media and content creation support, and event-driven engagements. Ambassadors like TenZ gain resources from Red Bull Media House to produce high-quality content such as documentaries, video features, and live streams, significantly amplifying both their personal brands and Red Bull’s reach.
“Joining Red Bull is a dream come true,” said TenZ. “I’ve always admired their commitment to pushing limits and achieving greatness. I can’t wait to show what we can accomplish together.”
The partnership includes exclusive content, live activations, and innovative projects, promising fans behind-the-scenes insights and dynamic esports experiences. These activities strategically enable Red Bull to deepen audience penetration among the highly coveted 18–34-year-old demographic, foster community trust, and create a robust pipeline of engaging storytelling.
Jérôme Coupez, Founder and CEO of Prodigy Agency, emphasized the significance of this deal: “It has been a long-term goal for TenZ, and I’m incredibly proud to have helped make it a reality.”
With TenZ on board, Red Bull expands its influential esports presence, reinforcing its strategic aim of building authentic brand connections within gaming’s vibrant culture.

articles.title: VALORANT Champion TenZ Joins Red Bull’s Competitive Roster - Inven Global
articles.content:
Red Bull has added VALORANT champion and content creator Tyson “TenZ” Ngo to its competitive gaming lineup, the company announced Tuesday. TenZ joins the Red Bull VALORANT roster alongside Tarik “tarik” Çelik, Melanie “meL” Hoi-San Man and the Sentinels organization.
With a combined following of nearly 11.8 million across social platforms, Ngo emerged as one of VALORANT’s most influential figures as the game’s popularity surged. His poised performances under high stakes helped Sentinels complete an undefeated run at VCT Masters Reykjavik in 2021, marking the first global LAN event in the game’s history and cementing his status as a leading competitor.
After stepping away from professional play at the close of 2024, TenZ has maintained his prominence as a top-ranked Twitch streamer and entrepreneur. He leveraged his esports reputation to launch a line of gaming peripherals, extending his reach into hardware design and consumer products. His continued success in streaming and merchandise reflects a growing trend of pro players who parlay in-game achievements into long-term brand partnerships.
TenZ’s career arc—from Counter-Strike prospect to VALORANT world champion—illustrates the evolving landscape of esports, where performance and personality intersect. His disciplined approach to practice and content creation resonates with a new generation of gamers seeking sustainable careers beyond competition. This philosophy aligns with Red Bull’s strategy to support talent capable of shaping the broader gaming culture.
Born May 5, 2001, in Vancouver, TenZ is 24 years old and holds Canadian citizenship. His precision aiming and calm demeanor have defined his playstyle, earning him recognition among peers and fans alike. As he transitions fully into content creation under Red Bull’s banner, TenZ is poised to influence both competitive circuits and online entertainment for years to come.

articles.title: TenZ becomes Red Bull’s latest athlete - Esports Insider
articles.content:
Red Bull has announced that Tyson ‘TenZ’ Ngo, one of VALORANT’s most popular esports figures, has joined as its latest athlete.
The Red Bull and TenZ partnership, facilitated by esports talent agency Prodigy Agency, will see the Twitch streamer collaborate with the energy drink brand on various activations. This includes exclusive content, projects, behind-the-scenes insights and live activities for fans to enjoy.
The former esports professional is widely regarded was one of the most influential players from the VALORANT scene. He is most well-known for his time with Sentinels, being part of the rosters that won Masters Reykjavik in 2021. However, he left the organisation in May 2024.
Since then, he has amassed over 14m followers across all media platforms, enjoying a new career as a content creator and streamer. However, he still remains somewhat active in the esports scene. Last month, for example, he temporarily joined Cubert Academy for VCT Challengers Stage 2.
“Joining Red Bull is a dream come true. I’ve always admired their commitment to pushing limits and achieving greatness, whether it’s in extreme sports, gaming, or high-energy experiences,” said TenZ.
“I can’t wait to show what we can accomplish together and share my journey with the incredible Red Bull community.”
With TenZ on board, Red Bull continues its strategic push in 2025 as it continues making bold moves in the competitive scene. From signing esports personalities, like League of Legends content creator Marc Robert ‘Caedrel’ Lamont, to hosting events such as the upcoming Tetris global esports tournament.
“This partnership between TenZ and Red Bull is a perfect match. It has been a long-term goal for TenZ, and I’m incredibly proud to have helped make it a reality,” said Jérôme Coupez, Founder and CEO of Prodigy Agency.
“I have no doubt that this collaboration will lead to some truly iconic moments in the world of esports and gaming.”
Prodigy Agency manages the careers of esports players, influencers, and gaming brands. Its talent network boasts over 60m followers. The agency has worked with brands such as Redbull, Meta, Tencent, and NetEase in several online campaigns.

articles.title: Ludwig, Tarik and TenZ to co-stream Red Bull Home Ground World Finals - Esports Insider
articles.content:
Creators ‘Ludwig‘ Ahgren, ‘Tarik‘ Çelik and Tysan ‘TenZ‘ Van Ngo will attend VALORANT’s Red Bull Home Ground World Final event as co-streamers.
The talent will be on-site watching the esports tournament at the Manhattan Centre in New York, US, from November 14th to 16th, 2025.
Meet The Co-Streamers
The creators themselves have a long history in esports. TenZ is well known for his run in VALORANT with Sentinels before his departure earlier this year, and is currently part of the Red Bull athlete programme.
Tarik is a retired Counter-Strike: Global Offensive player who, in the past, has played for organisations such as Evil Geniuses, MIBR, Cloud9 and OpTic Gaming. He currently works for Sentinels as one of the most popular streamers in VALORANT, and is an ambassador for gaming apparel brand H4X.
Ludwig is a well-known streamer known for organising competitive gaming and real-life events. He has worked with Red Bull Gaming in the past to create events such as the Streamer Games in Los Angeles, US. Earlier this year, he became a co-owner of Shopify Rebellion with fellow creator Charles ‘MoistCr1TiKal’ Christopher White Jr.
What is Red Bull Home Ground World Finals?
The Red Bull Home Ground World Final will take place as part of the VALORANT 2025 Off//Season. It is organised by energy drink brand Red Bull and is being held in partnership with Riot Games, the game’s developer.

articles.title: Alexis and TenZ join the Forbes US Games 30 under 30 list - Esports.gg
articles.content:
SRG Alexis and former pro TenZ made the 2025 Forbes US Games 30 Under 30 list as the only VALORANT players.
Sometimes, loving the gaming world can be hard, especially when other people’s judgments try to discredit our passions. However, some examples prove we’re not kids for loving video games. Shopify Rebellion Gold Alexis “alexis” Guarrasi and Tyson “TenZ” Ngo are two of them, and now they’ve been named to the Forbes US Games 30 Under 30 list.
Alexis and Tenz in the Forbes US Games 30 under 30 list
Among the many personalities and gaming figures out there, Alexis and TenZ were the only VALORANT professional players selected for the Forbes US Games 30 Under 30 list.
The highest-earning female player in VALORANT is one of the most influential pro players in the inclusive scenario. Earning over $150,000 in tournaments and 13 regional Game Changers championships, Alexis changed the lives of many young female players. She showed us that women can play the same video games as men and excel at them. Alexis brought her talent to the stage, breaking barriers and inspiring a generation to play boldly, unapologetically, and with pride.
On the other hand, TenZ has completely changed the FPS scene. With insane micro and macro skills, the Canadian player has drawn countless fans to international competitions just to watch him play. Like Alexis, he serves as an inspiration for many young players, several of whom are now professionals. TenZ won two Masters titles and one domestic title.
In 2024, TenZ retired from competitive play and is now a full-time content creator. TenZ is also very vocal about the game’s issues, serving as an agent of change for the FPS title’s continued growth over the years. Both of them have shaped the VALORANT scene, bringing pride and glory to one of the most beloved games in the genre.
The Forbes list

articles.title: Tenz partners with Pulsar Gaming to launch new wireless gaming mouse - Esports Insider
articles.content:
Hardware company Pulsar Gaming Gears and former esports player Tyson ‘TenZ’ Ngo have teamed up to launch a new gaming mouse.
Announced at the VALORANT Champion Tour (VCT) Americas Block Party, Pulsar collaborated with the content creator and VCT Americas’ official PC partner iBUYPOWER to sell a limited amount of the Pulsar TenZ Signature edition mice ahead of its April launch.
At a weight of only 47 grams, the wireless gaming mouse is stated to have an extended battery life, black-and-white visual aesthetics and an optimised mouse shape for comfortable daily use.
According to a release, iBUYPOWER will be the exclusive online retailer of the Pulsar TenZ Signature Edition wireless gaming mouse. The gaming gear is currently selling at a price of $130 (~£120.71). Starting in April, the mouse will become available for purchase on Pulsar.gg’s online store and other major retailers.
Founded in 2020 in South Korea, Pulsar Gaming Gears is the official mouse, keyboard and mousepad partner of the VCT Americas and VCT Pacific. The company has a strong focus on offering high-tech products at better cost performance and has quickly expanded its presence in Japan and China with dedicated branch offices.
Esports and Peripherals
Hardware partnerships between pro players and content creators are a known strategy in the esports space.
Earlier last month, hardware brand Razer unveiled the new gaming mouse in collaboration with League of Legends professional player Faker, launching the Razer Viper V3 Pro Faker Edition. The same brand has also worked with VALORANT players, having signed Zachary ‘zekken’ Patrone to test and provide feedback to products in development.
Stuart Chan, CMO at Pulsar Gaming Gears, commented on the collaboration: “With TenZ, we were given the opportunity to create a product that was originally incepted for one person, one hand, and a signature playstyle. It reinforced a core belief we have at Pulsar that everyone should have the right to gear fit for peak performance.
“The mouse is one of our most exciting products to date, and serves as a high benchmark for all future partnership products. TenZ was a true pleasure to work with and we’re looking forward to more potential collaborations in the future.”

articles.title: TenZ launches VALORANT Community Awards Show - Esports Insider
articles.content:
Former professional VALORANT player Tyson ‘TenZ‘ Van Ngo has revealed a community awards show for VALORANT esports.
The 2025 VALORANT Community Awards Show is a live ceremony celebrating the VALORANT Champions Tour (VCT) and Game Changers scenes.
The awards ceremony will take place in Los Angeles, California, on December 15th in collaboration with Riot Games and Red Bull. Fans can tune into the ceremony across TenZ’s Twitch and YouTube channels.
In addition to the date and location, the former Sentinels player shared that the finalists will be revealed at a later date. So far, the only award category confirmed is the Red Bull Clutch of the Year, with other categories being unveiled in the coming weeks.
VCT and Game Changers teams are also involved in the nominee selection process. Players and coaches will pick their top five nominees for each category using a point-based system. The three with the most points will become the finalists.
Since parting ways with Sentinels, TenZ has remained an active member of the VALORANT esports community. In November, TenZ attended the Red Bull Home Ground World Final event — which was won by G2 Esports — as a co-streamer.
TenZ is also no stranger to collaborating with Red Bull. In June, he became the latest esports personality to join the energy drink brand’s athlete programme, which continues to recruit players and content creators.
Award Ceremonies And Esports
Awards ceremonies focusing on a specific title are a growing trend within esports. October saw Supercell unveil the Clash Royale League 2025 Awards to celebrate the best moments from across the year.
Elsewhere, Eefje ‘Sjokz‘ Depoortere and Marc Robert ‘Caedrel‘ Lamont will host the second edition of The League Awards, marking notable achievements and moments from across the League of Legends esports ecosystem.
Released in 2020, VALORANT has cemented its place as one of the most popular esports titles in the world. In 2021, it won the Esports Game of the Year award at the Esports Awards, an annual ceremony celebrating the wider industry. 2025 saw the first-person shooter title fail to win an accolade after it missed out on Esports Game of the Year to League of Legends.

articles.title: TenZ says CS2 "feels like" VALORANT: "A lot of gunfights are decided based on RNG" - Dust2.us
articles.content:
TenZ says CS2 "feels like" VALORANT: "A lot of gunfights are decided based on RNG"
Former CS:GO pro turned VALORANT superstar Tyson "TenZ" Ngo was once very satisfied with CS2, but it turns out he drastically changed his mind about Valve's FPS.
During a recent livestream, TenZ compared CS2 to VALORANT in a negative way and explained why he isn't playing much CS2 nowadays.
"If CS:GO was still around, I probably would play a fair bit of CS:GO," TenZ said.
"I'm not too big of a fan of CS2. I find CS2 feels like VALORANT. In VALORANT a lot of gunfights are decided based on RNG, and you get running sh*t a lot, and the interp is really bad for online play."
TenZ carried on, explaining that some of the things he loved about CS:GO just don't work as much in CS2 like spray control and movement.
For TenZ, it was "absolutely amazing" to put hundreds or thousands of hours into mastering these aspects and get rewarded. Nowadays, he finds movement and spraying not as good and blames subtick for it.
"Subtick makes it a lot harder for you to bhop around and stuff," TenZ said.
"Spray control, being able to get a three-man spray down, is unbelievably satisfying, and then CS2 comes around and it basically becomes VALORANT. Bursting, tapping is way better, sprays are random feeling, you got run shit a lot, and players that aren't as good as you could f*ck you more often."
This is a considerable U-turn for TenZ in regard of what he thinks about CS2 as last year he said during a livestream that CS2 was more fun than VALORANT.

articles.title: TenZ officially departs from Sentinels - Esports.gg
articles.content:
TenZ is departing from Sentinels after nearly four years of dedication. The Canadian player described the team as a true family.
Tyson “TenZ” Ngo announced his departure from Sentinels on May 8. He is regarded as one of the best VALORANT players and retired in September 2024 after many years in the professional first-person shooter (FPS) scene. TenZ had been a part of the Sentinels organization since 2021.
TenZ leaves Sentinels
In a heartfelt post on X, TenZ reflected on his time with Sentinels, calling it “an amazing ride” with people he considers “true family.” The Canadian player shared that while the announcement is “a little bittersweet,” he is excited for the next chapter in his life. He thanked all of the Sentinels’ fans for their support and encouraged them to keep cheering, even without him. “All good things must come to an end. Goodbye, Sen City; it’s been fun!” TenZ wrote.
Tenz leaves behind a career featuring two major titles: the Masters Reykjavik in 2021 and the Masters Madrid in 2024, along with domestic titles and offseason tournaments. The player has been focusing on streaming VALORANT on Twitch, which means you can still follow him and see him play.
“Sentinels is the best North American organization you could be a part of,” Tenz stated in a clip shared by the organization on X. The Canadian player went on to explain that he still has “the key to the office” and knows he will always be welcomed to revisit the staff and players. “We are a f****** family!” he said.
Future sponsors
Sentinels has clarified the reasons for TenZ’s departure. The organization states that this choice is solely due to a conflict with future sponsorship deals. “Guys, relax, this is just to avoid any conflicts with future sponsors. TenZ will always be part of the Sentinels family,” the organization wrote.
Fans have been sharing their respect and appreciation for TenZ all over social media. “Hard time for a TenZ glazer and SEN fan,” a fan said. “Wait, this makes me so emotional,” another one wrote. Many are even calling it “the end of an era.” Nevertheless, many fans are still emphasizing that, no matter his choice, they will always support him and his work.
Be sure to check out TenZ’s top ten epic plays of all time. Although he is leaving the organization, his legacy will continue to influence the esports industry. Thank you for everything, TenZ!

articles.title: TenZ Officially Parts Ways With Sentinels - Hotspawn
articles.content:
Former VALORANT professional player and now content creator Tyson “TenZ” Ngo has confirmed his departure from esports organisation Sentinels.
The Canadian streamer has confirmed he will be leaving the organization on May 8 after making a post on X. In the message to his community, TenZ described his time on Sentinals as “an amazing ride” and that he “wouldn’t have traded it for anything else”, calling the players and staff “true family”.
“I appreciate all the Sentinels fans for the continued support throughout my career and hope you continue to support the team even with my absence. All good things must come to an end, goodbye Sen City, it’s been fun!” he wrote.
The announcement confirms the speculations from the previous days when members of the VALORANT community noticed TenZ’s social media pages no longer were affiliated with the esports organization.
Sentinels quickly clarified the reasons behind the departure, stating that the decision was made solely due to a conflict with future sponsorship deals. “Guys, relax, this is just to avoid any conflicts with future sponsors. TenZ will always be part of the Sentinels family,” the organization wrote on X.
Despite no longer being with Sentinels, TenZ has stated he will be open to future collaborations on content and even joked about still having access to the team’s office.
TenZ is regarded as one of the best VALORANT players in the early years of the competitive scene. Joining Sentinels back in 2021 after transitioning from CS:GO, he led the team to two international titles, Masters Reykjavik in 2021 and Masters Madrid in 2024, as well as a fourth place at last year’s VCT Champions Seoul. Shortly after the end of the tournament, TenZ announced his retirement from competitive on September 14th, 2024, moving to streaming on Twitch.

articles.title: "All good things must come to an end": TenZ announces departure from Sentinels - Esports Insider
articles.content:
VALORANT veteran Tyson ‘TenZ’ Ngo announced earlier today that he was leaving Sentinels after four years on the team.
On X (formerly Twitter), TenZ sent a message to fans: “I’m sure most of you have seen now and yes, I have parted ways with Sentinels. It was an amazing ride and I wouldn’t have traded it for anything else.”
Why Is TenZ Leaving Sentinels?
TenZ was one of the first well-known VALORANT players, having changed to Riot’s tactical shooter in 2020 after a career in Counter-Strike. While playing on loan for Sentinels, TenZ became one of the first rosters to win a VALORANT Masters event after a victory at Masters Reykjavik in 2021. The team continued to find success, winning VALORANT Masters Madrid in 2024.
Later that year, TenZ announced that he was going to retire from competitive VALORANT and would become a content creator for Sentinels. At the time, TenZ explained that he had ‘a lot of stuff’ he wanted to do outside of the game that he felt ‘very ambitious about.’ He has currently amassed over 6.5 million followers across Twitch and YouTube.
Now, TenZ is leaving Sentinels altogether. In his tweet, the FPS star claimed he was ‘excited for this new chapter’ but he didn’t specify exactly what his plans were. The VALORANT community, including fellow pro players, responded with sadness over TenZ departure, but seemed curious to know what was next.
Meanwhile, Sentinels hasn’t announced anything on their end. Sentinels currently has a full competitive roster but it’s possible the organisation could sign a new streamer.

The three-day event marks the second edition of Home Ground, where teams from three of T1’s flagship esports divisions face off against invited opponents in front of their home crowd. This year’s event will take place at INSPIRE Arena, the 15,000-seat venue that previously hosted the 2024 VALORANT Champions Seoul Finals and saw EDward Gaming lift the trophy.
T1’s LCK, LCK Challengers, and VCT squads will all be in action throughout the event, with the VALORANT segment scheduled for Saturday, July 26, featuring a VCT Pacific match and two showmatches. articles.title: TenZ is the most visited VALORANT player on Liquipedia in 2024 - Esports Insider
articles.content:
Tyson ‘TenZ‘ Ngo, Sentinels’ recently retired star player, has once again claimed the title of the most visited VALORANT player on Liquipedia in 2024.
In terms of organisations, Sentinels remains the most visited VALORANT team, followed by VCT Pacific powerhouse, Paper Rex.
Ever since entering the VALORANT competitive scene with Cloud9 in 2020, the Canadian quickly became the face of VALORANT esports, in no small part due to his plays on Jett. In June 2021, TenZ was purchased by Sentinels for a reported buyout between $1.25m to $1.5m.
He led Sentinels to victory at VALORANT Masters Reykjavík 2021, securing the title of tournament MVP and lifting the game’s first-ever international trophy. Not only that, but TenZ was also the first player to reach the VALORANT rank—now known as Radiant—and the first North American to win two Masters titles, the second being Masters Madrid 2024.
Before announcing his retirement in September 2024, he competed in VALORANT Champions 2024, marking the final event of his career. However, he is still signed with Sentinels as a content creator, focusing on streaming and watch-partying Sentinels matches.
Following TenZ in Liquipedia’s 2024 most-visited players list is MIBR’s Aspas, who climbed eight spots from 2023. Additionally, the list features two more Sentinels players, zekken and johnqt, in the top 10.
A major highlight of the rankings is Florescent breaking into the top five, becoming the only former Game Changers player to enter the list. Florescent recently made history as the first-ever GC player to enter VCT and is currently competing for 2024 EMEA Ascension winners, Apeks.

articles.title: “Precise gunplay? It’s f—ing Power Rangers:” TenZ on VALORANT’s utility dominated meta - Esports Insider
articles.content:
VALORANT was launched with the goal of offering precise gunplay while integrating agent abilities to add an extra layer of strategic gameplay. However, over time, as new agents and abilities were introduced, the balance shifted, with utilities overpowering aiming skills.
Not only has this made the game more challenging for beginners, but it has also left players helpless in situations where they get overwhelmed by utility spam. This has contributed to the rise of the retake meta, especially with the introduction of agents like Tejo and Waylay.
Multiple players and streamers, including Tyson ‘TenZ‘ Ngo, widely referred to as the face of VALORANT, have expressed frustration over the utility-heavy nature of the game.
TenZ Criticizes the Current State of VALORANT
During a recent stream, TenZ reacted to clips showcasing the overwhelming utility dumps defenders were facing, including flashes, recon abilities, ultimates, and more, one after the other.
“Look at this f—ing shit, what’s going on? Red, green, blue, dead, dead,” he said in frustration.
“This is f—ing Power Rangers, bro. Do you see that? They used all their special moves on the same player!”
When a viewer asked about ways to counter utility-heavy rushes, TenZ responded: “If they want the site, they’re gonna take the site. There’s nothing you can do to stop them. So, you might as well fall back, play retake, and rely on numbers. That’s the only way to counter it.”
A few days ago, TenZ even mentioned on X (Twitter) sarcastically that he sometimes feels that his color blindness is momentarily cured because of all the colors on his screen.
“VALORANT wasn’t like this before. Obviously, moving shots, jump kills, and spam kills happen. But my issue is the sheer dominance of utilities. I feel like utilities should complement precise gunplay, rather than just giving you trauma,” he added.
Responding to TenZ’s concerns on X, Alex Wheeler, Principal UX Designer at Riot Games, stated that the team is actively monitoring the situation and working on making improvements. However, no timeline has been provided at the moment for potential changes.

articles.title: Top 5 esports streamers to watch in 2025 - Esports Insider
articles.content:
Esports streamers are becoming more popular as the competitive scene continues to grow, featuring retired and active athletes alike.
From legendary gameplay to engaging content, these five esports streamers are shaping the future of competitive gaming and content culture.
TenZ Is a VALORANT Pro Turned Esport Streamer
Jared ‘TenZ‘ Latham is primarily known for his exceptional skills in VALORANT, balancing insights on the latest updates with variety content.
A former member of Cloud9, TenZ rose to fame after joining Sentinels on loan in 2021, leading the team to victory at VCT Masters Reykjavik, the first international VALORANT tournament.
He has since stepped away from the competitive spotlight to pursue streaming and content creation, partly because of the utility-driven direction he foresaw VALORANT taking. Still, this hasn’t stopped him from grinding VALORANT in his streams, amassing over 4.3m followers on Twitch.
Shroud Is a Former CS Pro Turned Esport Org Owner
Michael ‘Shroud‘ Grzesiek is arguably the most well-known retired esport athlete turned streamer. He’s built a reputation for his incredible aim in shooters such as Apex Legends, Call of Duty, and most recently Marvel Rivals.
Known for his exceptional plays during the peak of Counter-Strike: Global Offensive, he helped organisations like Cloud9 and Sentinel achieve great success across several tournaments.
He became even more influential when he decided to hang up the jersey to pursue streaming, going as far as starting his own esports organisation, Shroud-X. He now has 11.1m followers on Twitch, where he is known for his incredible FPS skills but also dabbling in casual games to provide commentary.
Beaulo Amongst the Best R6 Esport Streamers and Pros
Jason ‘Beaulo‘ Doty is a prominent figure in Rainbow Six Siege esports and is widely celebrated by the community as one of the best players in his prime.
Beaulo’s best feat came in 2022 when he and his team, TSM, won the Six Invitational 2022. He’s also consistently contributed towards TSM regularly qualifying for most international tournaments.
Previously, Beaulo had retired in early 2023 but returned later that year to play for DarkZero Esports. On March 5, 2025, he announced his second retirement. He has 1.3m followers on Twitch, but this number will likely grow as he focuses on streaming rather than the esports grind.
Faker Is One of the Best LoL Esports Streamers and Pros
In League of Legends, one of the best esports players turned streamer is Lee ‘Faker‘ Sang-hyeok. While Faker is still actively playing professionally for T1 as a midlaner, his popularity has grown behind the scenes as a content creator.
Faker is a three-time Worlds champion, winning 2013 (where he was awarded MVP), 2015, and 2016. He’s also won multiple LCK titles during his time with T1.
Faker’s League of Legends achievements have made him an icon in esports, allowing him to collaborate with well-known gaming brands such as Razer. He currently boasts 3.9m followers on Twitch, where he streams high-level League of Legends and provides behind-the-scenes discussions on the esports scene.
Clix Is A Well-Known Fortnite Esport Streamer and Co-Owner
Cody ‘Clix‘ Conrod is one of the most well-known professional Fortnite players and streamers, rising to fame thanks to his mechanical skills in the battle royale mode.
Clix became widely recognized after joining the esports organisation Misfits Gaming, and later becoming part of NRG Esports. He’s placed highly in international tournaments such as FNCS.
Nowadays he’s a top content creator and streamer, alongside being the co-owner of the North American esports organisation XSET. With 8.1m followers on Twitch, Clix has continued to entertain the Fortnite community even when not competing.

articles.title: 5 best VALORANT crosshair codes - Inven Global
articles.content:
Crosshair codes in VALORANT allow players to easily share their configurations with each other. Considering the game allows a great deal of customization in this regard, you can run into creative options, but you may want to pick the best VALORANT crosshair out of all if you're a competitive player.
There are plenty of abilities and animations in VALORANT, and it can get a bit chaotic in matches. When I first started playing first-person shooters decades ago, I had a habit of losing track of my crosshair in the midst of all the action. That's no longer the case, though, especially in VALORANT, since you can copy crosshairs quickly and test out combinations that work for you.
If you don't know where to start with crosshairs, we've compiled the five best VALORANT crosshairs of pro players in this article, and they should give you a jump start.
5. Alfajer's crosshair
Alfajer is one of the most consistent VALORANT pros in the world. He puts on great performances regardless of the stage, and he has a rather simplistic crosshair. Alfajer prefers a closed crosshair with neutral colors, which can be great for sniping.
Alfajer’s VALORANT Crosshair: 0;P;h;0;0t;1;0l;4;0o;1;0a;1;0f;0;1t;3;1o;2;1a;1;1m;0;1f;
4. Aspas' crosshair
Aspas rose to stardom after winning the VALORANT Champions 2022. He's a key player in South America and helped shape the region as one of the top competitors globally. When it comes to his crosshair preferences, Aspas prefers a classic red configuration that can also be considered small.
This red crosshair is relatively easy to keep track of amidst all the action, and it's a classic configuration amongst long-time players.
Aspas’ VALORANT Crosshair: 0;P;c;7;h;0;0l;3;0o;2;0a;1;0f;0;1b;
3. Zekken's crosshair
Zekken's an NA player who is known for his confident duelist playstyle. His crosshair also reflects his style, as it's a staple choice amongst duelist players and riflers in Counter-Strike terms.
Zekken’s VALORANT Crosshair: 0;P;c;1;o;1;d;1;0b;0;1b;0
2. TenZ's crosshair
TenZ may not be an active player in VALORANT's competitive scene, but he still streams his gameplay often. His broadcast attracts considerable attention, with an average viewership of thousands.
TenZ rolls out with a simple white crosshair, which is an excellent alternative for duelist mains.
TenZ’s VALORANT Crosshair: 0;s;1;P;c;5;h;0;m;1;0l;4;0o;2;0a;1;0f;0;1b;0
1. Derke's crosshair
Derke's a powerhouse of a VALORANT player. The duelist has provided significant value to the teams he has played for, and he's also an active communicator. When it comes to Derke's crosshair preferences, he opts for the color yellow while keeping the default style at a smaller size.
Derke’s VALORANT Crosshair: 0;P;c;1;o;1;f;0;0l;4;0o;2;0a;1;0f;0;1b;
How we chose the top 5 VALORANT crosshair codes
We prioritized consistency, visibility, and simplicity while choosing the best VALORANT crosshair codes. All the configurations on our list belong to professional players, who often finalize their setups after countless hours of play, testing what works best.
These crosshairs can be considered popular just because pros use them. However, they're still reliable configurations that help players perform well across different maps and situations.

articles.title: TenZ announces departure from Sentinels - Valorant - Gamereactor UK
articles.content:
After four years of working with the organisation.
HQ
When Valorant esports first took off, there were a handful of players that really caught the attention of many around the world, with one of these folk being Tyson "TenZ" Ngo. After proving to be a massive talent with Cloud9 Blue, he soon moved and joined Sentinels, where the pair acquired a bunch of trophies and tournament wins over the years. However, back in 2024, TenZ decided to step away from competitive play to instead take on a content creation role at Sentinels, although this is now coming to an end too.
In a post on X, TenZ notes that he is leaving the Sentinels organisation to instead pursue a new chapter in his life. The exact nature of this has not been confirmed as of yet, but we are told by TenZ:
"Sentinels was a true family for me in the players and the staff. A little bittersweet but I'm excited for this new chapter of my life. I appreciate all the Sentinels fans for the continued support throughout my career and hope you continue to support the team even with my absence. All good things must come to an end, goodbye Sen City it's been fun!"
